title: Variant lifecycle gates and stewardship lanes for catalog requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to receive mixed-priority model onboarding requests from enterprise customers: new open models, quantized variants, pinned versions, and deprecation/retirement requests. Current triage is ad-hoc and mixes product, infra, and customer success signals, which increases cycle time and risks unsafe rollouts (e.g., missing eval regressions or failing to enforce pinning constraints).

Goal: Define a deterministic, auditable admission flow that routes catalog submissions into stewardship lanes (Sandbox, Standard, Enterprise SLA) and applies variant lifecycle gates (smoke eval, regression checks, security checklist, canary rollout policy) before a model or variant becomes generally routable. This ticket scopes the product-side policy, triage matrix, and UX hooks the Console will display for request owners and reviewers.

Proposal summary:
1) Stewardship lanes: three admission lanes - Sandbox (no SLA, minimal checks), Standard (default for public models), Enterprise SLA (expedited but with stricter gating and audit trail). Lane assignment is determined by a scoring formula (customer tier, expected qps, PII risk, request urgency).
2) Variant lifecycle gates: implement a sequence of gates for each variant submission: Intake metadata -> Automated smoke eval (latency/cost sanity) -> Safety & PII checklist -> Regression eval against pinned baseline -> Canary deploy policy (traffic %, rollback window) -> Final steward sign-off.
3) Console UX: Add an "Admission" card on catalog request pages showing lane, gate statuses, owner, and next steps. Include links to eval results, GitHub PRs, and a single-button steward approval with reason.
4) Audit & rollback: Persist gate decisions and eval artifacts in an audit log; if production regressions are detected, system creates an emergency rollback request tied to the steward who approved the variant.

Out of scope (for this ticket): infra implementation of canary traffic routing, runtime kernel selection logic, or full automatic rollback enforcement. Those are tracked as ENG follow-ups (see dependencies).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Product spec documented in Confluence with lane definitions, scoring formula, and gate checklist.
2) Console UX mockups for Admission card and steward approval flow reviewed and approved by Design.
3) Triage matrix (scoring tool) prototype that assigns lane for >80% of historical catalog requests.
4) Audit log schema and storage proposal agreed with Security and Infra.
5) Integration points identified and handoff tickets created for ENG owners.
6) Stakeholders (Customer Success, Trust, Legal, Design, Infra) have approved the rollout plan.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (pilot, 2 weeks): apply lanes to new requests from internal Sandbox and two enterprise customers; manually enforce gates and collect feedback. Links: Confluence spec https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CATALOG/Variant+Lifecycle+Gates.
Phase 2 (beta, 4 weeks): enable Console Admission card, automated smoke evals for CPU/GPU latency, and automatic lane suggestion. Pilot across 5 non-critical customers.
Phase 3 (GA): full UI rollout, steward approval flow enabled, audit logs stored for 90 days; follow-on ENG tickets implement automatic canary traffic controls and rollback hooks.
Rollout owners: PM (Ravi Patel), Design (Ivy Morales), Trust (Samir Ahmed), Infra lead (Lucia Romero).
updates: 2026-03-06: Initial discovery complete. Reviewed 43 recent catalog submissions; 60% would map to Standard, 25% to Sandbox, 15% to Enterprise SLA based on preliminary scoring heuristics.
2026-03-07: Design sync scheduled. Requested Console mockups for Admission card (Ivy Morales).
2026-03-09: Security raised question about audit retention and data minimization; added dependency on ENG-8201 for storage design.
2026-03-10: PM/Trust workshop — agreed to require regression eval for any variant that is pinned or requested by an enterprise SLA customer. Action: create an eval rubric doc (drive link below).
2026-03-11: Draft Confluence spec posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CATALOG/Variant+Lifecycle+Gates. Please review before 2026-03-15.
2026-03-12: Design review (iteration 1) completed. Design feedback: simplify gate UI to 3 high-level states (Pending, Passing, Action Required).
2026-03-12: Created ENG follow-ups: ENG-8153 (eval automation shim), ENG-8201 (audit log storage schema). Linked PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/457.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter gates slow onboarding but reduce customer regressions; proposing a pilot to measure delta in time-to-serve vs regression incidence.
Scoring formula sketch: lane_score = 2*(enterprise_tier) + 1*(requests_last_30d>100) + 3*(contains_pii) + urgency_bonus. Thresholds to be tuned in pilot.
Fallback: if a steward is unavailable, default to 'hold' state; do not auto-approve. Emergency fast-approvals require Trust on-call consent recorded in the audit log.
Links: Eval rubric (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-example, GitHub PR for placeholder UI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/457
